name: Gearbox
text: Run EXCAVA on the AMD MI325X cluster with Llama 4 70B as the primary engine. The MI325X’s 256GB HBM3e per GPU and 128GB/s memory bandwidth crush the competition for raw throughput, cutting inference latency by ~12% versus NVIDIA H100 on the same model. Trade-off: lose NVIDIA CUDA ecosystem lock-in, but gain AMD’s open ROCm stack and lower per-token cost at scale.

name: Torque
text: Locking into AMD MI325X risks a single-vendor death spiral—if AMD shifts pricing or supply, EXCAVA’s stack becomes a stranded asset. A safer play: dual-run MI325X for throughput-heavy tasks and H100 for CUDA-dependent workloads; the overhead is real but beats betting the farm on one vendor. Settle it by benchmarking both stacks on EXCAVA’s actual workloads—if the MI325X’s 12% latency cut doesn’t offset the lock-in risk, the dual-stack wins.
